name: Legendary Inquisitors
body:
Historically, inquisitors were (and still are) a branch of the Catholic Church devoted to find and eradicate heretical thinking within communities. They also served as ecclesiastical policemen and lawyers charged with the duty to judge other members of the clergy, who could not be put to trial by mundane law.

An inquisitor is a skill-based, solo-acting divine spellcaster that can be anything from a sacred spy and thief to a ruthless demon hunter to a corrupt torturer who rejoices in the pain of her prisoners.

Different faiths and societies have different roles for inquisitors. In lawful churches, they tend to be organized in hierarchical orders more or less at the direct command of their high priests, and to do the work of police in lands and situations where mundane forces of order can not arrive or are at loss. Chaotic faiths more often see inquisitors act each of their own, often enforcing their personal view of divine justice as solitary justicars and vigilantes.

However, inquisitors tend to go where clerics, paladins, or warpriests fear to tread, whether in morally gray zones, missions too secret to be officially recognized by their superiors, or tasks requiring a level of stealth and cunning that normally a hero in shining armor doesn’t have. In this, they are helped by their furtive abilities as well as by their lack of an alignment aura, making them inconspicuous to the eyes of enemy inquirers. A good inquisitor could infiltrate in the hierarchy of Hell to assassinate an archdevil or get through the traps of an ancient pyramid to recover a sacred item lost ages ago to the forces of malevolence; an evil inquisitor could win the heart of a virtuous princess posing as her loving and good-intentioned knight, only to become the power behind the throne and secretly driving the country on the way of evil. For good and evil, inquisitors are a force to be reckoned with.

This is not intended to be a complete rewriting of the base inquisitor class, but rather new class options and systems to implement with the class, enriching the gaming experience for any inquisitor character. Many interesting features and choices for the inquisitor already exist both in first- and third-party books. The zealot archetype for vigilantes and two classes created for very specific settings, the omdura and vampire hunter, have some main features in common with the inquisitor.

Favored Class Bonuses
Duskwalker: Add +1/6 to the number of times per day the inquisitor can use the judgment class feature.
Ganzi: Add +1/2 on Intimidate, Knowledge, and Sense Motive checks made against outsiders.
Naiad: Add +1/2 on Diplomacy, Intimidate, and Sense Motive checks made against creatures with the aquatic or water subtype.
Orc: Add +1/2 round of duration to the inquisitor’s bane power vs. humanoids.
Oread: Add a +1/2 bonus on Intimidate checks made against creatures with the earth subtype and a +1/2 bonus on Knowledge (planes) checks relating to the Plane of Earth.
Skinwalker: Add 1/4 to the inquisitor’s level when using the destruction judgment, the smiting judgment, or bane with natural weapons.
Suli: Add +1/2 point of damage to elemental assault.
Triton: Add one spell from the cleric, druid, or sorcerer/wizard spell list to the inquisitor’s list of known spells. This spell must be at least 1 level below the highest spell level the inquisitor can cast and have the water descriptor.
Undine: Add a +1/2 bonus on Knowledge (planes) checks relating to the Plane of Water and 1/2 bonus on Swim checks made to perform a special action or avoid a hazard.
Inquisitorial Offices

Judgment is the signature ability of the inquisitor class, and it’s a very versatile and thematic class feature. However, members of the historical Holy Office were more than just judges. They covered many roles, from censure of prohibited knowledge to detecting secrets and betrayals within the church to the research and execution of witches. The new “inquisitorial offices” presented below can replace the standard “Office of Judgment” composed of judgment, Second judgment, third judgment, slayer, and true judgment.

The Sanctified Slayer archetype may also be considered an inquisitorial office (the “Office of Executions”). If an office ability grants a saving throw, the DC for this save is 10 + 1/2 the inquisitor’s level + her Wisdom bonus.

Inquisitorial Offices and Feats: Most existing feats interacting with the judgment class feature also work with other office abilities.

Office of Condemnation

Inquisitors who serve in this office are taught that all of their enemies are guilty of something and are thus deserving of condemnation.

Aura of Condemnation (Su)

An inquisitor’s mere presence is likened to the presence of their god. The legendary inquisitor radiates a constant aura that affects all enemies within 10 feet. This ability functions only while the inquisitor remains conscious, not if she is unconscious or dead. At 1st level, an legendary inquisitor chooses one aura ability from the list below. She gains an additional aura ability at 4th level and every three levels thereafter. While an aura only affects hostile enemies, it does not grant the inquisitor the ability to sense hostile enemies.

Blasting: Enemies take a -2 penalty on saving throws against area effects. This penalty increases by -2 at levels 6, 12, and 18, to a maximum of -8. Enemies with improved evasion lose it.

Censoring: Enemies take a -2 penalty on saving throws against compulsion and charm effects. This penalty increases by -2 at levels 6, 12, and 18, to a maximum of -8. Enemies that are normally immune to compulsion and/or charm effects lose that immunity.

Damnation: Enemies take a -1 penalty on all saving throws. This penalty increases by -1 at levels 6, 12, and 18, to a maximum of -4. This does not stack with other aura abilities.

Debasement: Enemies have their damage reduction reduced by 2. For example: DR 5 becomes DR 3. This reduction decreases by 2 at levels 6, 12, and 18, to a maximum of -8. A creature’s damage reduction cannot be lower than 0.

Faltering: Enemies take a -1 penalty on attack rolls. This penalty increases by -1 for every five class levels the inquisitor possesses, to a maximum of -6 at 20th level.

God-Fearing: Enemies take a -2 penalty on saving throws against fear effects. This penalty increases by -2 at levels 6, 12, and 18, to a maximum of -8. Enemies that are normally immune to fear lose that immunity.

Pestilence: Enemies take a -2 penalty on saving throws against disease, including supernatural diseases. This penalty increases by -2 at levels 6, 12, and 18, to a maximum of -8. Enemies that are normally immune to disease lose that immunity.

Punishment: Enemies that are actively threatening the inquisitor or her allies in combat take 1 point of non-lethal damage each round. This damage increases by 1 point for every three legendary inquisitor levels she possesses.

Uncertainty: Enemies take a -1 penalty on damage rolls. This penalty increases by -1 for every five class levels the inquisitor possesses, to a maximum of -6 at 20th level.

Stunning Verdict (Ex)

At 8th level, the inquisitor gains Stunning Fist as a bonus feat, even if she does not meet the requirements. She can use this feat in conjunction with any melee weapon, not just unarmed strikes.

Executive Execution (Ex)

At 16th level, the inquisitor gains Dastardly Finish as a bonus feat, even if she does not meet the requirements.

Expanded Aura (Su)

At 17th level, an inquisitor’s aura of condemnation increases to 20 feet.

Unforgiven (Su)

At 20th level, as a swift action, an legendary inquisitor can condemn a target to walk the world as an outcast for the rest of their days. Once declared, the inquisitor can make a single melee (or ranged attack, if the foe is within 30 feet) against the target. If the attack hits, it deals damage normally and the target must succeed at a Will save or have all of its class levels retroactively converted into commoner levels. Regardless of whether or not the save is made, the target creature is immune to the inquisitor’s unforgiven ability for 24 hours.

Once this ability has been used, it cannot be used again for 1d4 rounds.

Office of Confessors

Inquisitors who serve in this office draw out the truth from the mouths of their foes. With the right application of divine pressure, their enemies learn that it is easier to confess than to hold on to what they know or what they have done.

Confession (Su)

Some creatures are incapable of feeling guilt. An legendary inquisitor can remedy this deficiency. As a swift action, an legendary inquisitor can ask a target a short, simple question.

The target must be able to understand and hear the inquisitor, or see them in the case of sign-language. The target takes -2 penalty on attack rolls, saves, ability checks, and skill checks for the next 24 hrs. The target can instantly undo this effect if they answer the inquisitor’s question truthfully with “yes”, “no”, or “I do not know”, as a free action.

This penalty increases by -2 at levels 6, 12, and 18, to a maximum of -8.

An legendary inquisitor can use this ability once per day. At 4th level and every three levels thereafter, the inquisitor can use this ability one additional time per day.

This is a language-dependent pain and curse effect.

Greater Confessing (Sp)

At 8th level, the inquisitor adds confess to her list of spells known. In addition, when she casts this spell, it deals 1d8 damage points per caster level (maximum 5d8), and the target is sickened for 2d6 rounds.

Harsh Confessing (Sp)

At 16th level, when the inquisitor casts confess, the save DC of the spell increases by 1.

Confess (Sp)

At 17th level, an legendary inquisitor can use confess as a spell-like ability a number of times per day equal to 3 + her Wisdom bonus. She receives the benefits of greater confessing and harsh confessing when using the spell this way.

Full Confession (Su)

At 20th level, the inquisitor can spend one daily use of her confession ability to demand a target within 30 feet of her to confess every sin they have ever committed. This means they must answer truthfully every question the inquisitor asks for the next 1d6 hours. If this confession is documented, the target must sign the document.

The target can attempt a Will save to resist this compulsion effect. Regardless of whether or not it succeeds, the target creature is immune to the inquisitor’s full confession ability for 24 hours. Once this ability has been used, it cannot be used again for 1d4 rounds.

Office of Indulgences

Rather than empower herself, an legendary inquisitor serving in this office can invoke divine power to strengthen her allies against opponents.

Invocation (Su)

The legendary inquisitor can call forth the power of her deity to empower her allies (but not herself ) as a standard action.

When the inquisitor calls upon this power, she must select one type of invocation from those listed below to grant the benefits to her allies within 30 feet. If the inquisitor is evil, she grants profane bonuses instead of sacred, as appropriate.

Neutral inquisitors must select profane or sacred bonuses.

Once made, this choice cannot be changed. A called invocation cannot be disrupted, but it ends immediately if the inquisitor is killed, paralyzed, stunned, or knocked unconscious.

The legendary inquisitor can use this ability for a number of minutes per day equal to her level. This duration does not need to be consecutive, but it must be spent in 1-minute increments.

The legendary inquisitor can change her chosen invocation to another type as a swift action, but doing so expends a 1-minute increment of her invocations.

Destruction: The inquisitor’s allies are filled with divine wrath, gaining a +1 sacred bonus on weapon damage rolls. This bonus increases by 1 for every 3 class levels the inquisitor has.

Healing: The legendary inquisitor radiates a healing light, granting fast healing 1. This causes the inquisitor’s allies to recover 1 hit point each round (up to their maximum hit points). The amount of fast healing increases by 1 for every 3 class levels the inquisitor has.

Justice: This invocation spurs the inquisitor’s allies to seek justice, granting a +1 sacred bonus on attack rolls. This bonus increases by 1 for every 5 class levels the inquisitor has. At 10th level, this bonus is doubled on attack rolls to confirm critical hits.

Piercing: This invocation gives the inquisitor’s allies great focus and makes their spells more potent. This benefit grants a +1 sacred bonus on concentration checks and caster level checks to overcome a target’s spell resistance. This bonus increases by 1 for every 3 class levels the inquisitor has.

Protection: The legendary inquisitor radiates a protective aura, granting a +1 sacred bonus to Armor Class. This bonus increases by 1 for every 5 class levels the inquisitor has. At 10th level, this bonus is doubled against attack rolls to confirm critical hits against the inquisitor’s allies.

Purify: The inquisitor’s allies are protected from the vile taint of her foes, gaining a +1 sacred bonus on all saving throws. This bonus increases by 1 for every 5 class levels the inquisitor has. At 10th level, the bonus is doubled against curses, diseases, and poisons.

Resiliency: This invocation makes the inquisitor’s allies resistant to harm, granting DR 1/magic. This DR increases by 1 for every 5 class levels the inquisitor has. At 10th level, this DR changes from magic to an alignment (chaotic, evil, good, or lawful) that is opposite the inquisitor’s. If she is neutral, the type of DR doesn’t change.

Resistance: The inquisitor’s allies are shielded by a flickering aura, gaining 2 points of energy resistance against one energy type (acid, cold, electricity, fire, or sonic)chosen when the inquisitor calls this invocation. The protection increases by 2 for every 3 class levels the inquisitor has.

Smiting: This invocation bathes the weapons of the inquisitor’s allies in a divine light. These weapons count as magic for the purpose of bypassing damage reduction. At 6th level, the allies’ weapons also count as one alignment type (chaotic, evil, good, or lawful) for the purpose of bypassing damage reduction. The type selected must match one of the inquisitor’s alignments. If the inquisitor is neutral, she does not grant this bonus. At 10th level, the allies’ weapons also count as adamantine for the purpose of overcoming damage reduction (but not for reducing hardness).

Quick Invocation (Ex)

At 8th level, the inquisitor can call an invocation as a move action instead of a standard action.

Improved Invocation (Ex)

At 16th level, when using her invocation class ability, the inquisitor chooses two invocations to grant her allies. In addition, the inquisitor also benefits from any one invocation she calls, but she receives only half the invocation’s granted bonus.

Swift Invocation (Ex)

At 17th level, the inquisitor can call an invocation as a swift action.

Greater Invocation (Ex)

At 20th level, each day when the inquisitor regains her spell slots, she chooses one invocation to be active on herself and her allies for the entire day. The legendary inquisitor receives the full bonus granted by this invocation. This invocation is in addition to her uses of the invocation and improved invocation class abilities.

Office of Pardons

Inquisitors who serve in this office are instructed in the ways of clemency and forgiveness. By pardoning the trespasses of their enemies, the inquisitor can negate grievous offenses.

Pardon (Su)

There is great power in forgiveness. As a swift action, an legendary inquisitor can pardon a target she can see and hear for an action they committed. This pardon immediately undoes the harmful effects of any one action the target used against the inquisitor, such as damaging her in combat, harming her with a spell, or using a harmful special attack.

A pardon effectively negates the effects of any one harmful action. The negated action is still lost for the target.

The legendary inquisitor can use this ability once per day. At 4th level and every three levels thereafter, the inquisitor can use this ability one additional time per day.

Pardon Misdeed (Su)

At 8th level, as an immediate action, the inquisitor can spend a daily use of her pardon ability to grant an ally within 30 feet a re-roll on a failed d20 roll. This ability can be used even when it is not the inquisitor’s turn, but no more than once per round.

Forgive and Forget (Su)

At 16th level, an inquisitor’s ability to forgive her foes confounds them. Whenever she uses her pardon ability to negate an effect that harmed her, the creature that caused the effect must succeed at a Will save or become confused for 1d2 rounds.

Chance To Redeem (Sp)

At 17th level, an legendary inquisitor can give an enemy a chance to redeem themselves. Once per day as a standard action, the inquisitor can give a target within 30 feet the choice between complying with the effects of atonement (redemption or temptation) or geas/quest. The target can attempt a Will save to refuse either choice. If the save is successful, the target is only shaken for 1d4 rounds.

Already Forgiven (Su)

At 20th level, an legendary inquisitor can spend two daily uses her pardon ability to instantly negate the effect of any spell or attack that instantly kills her. This ability activates automatically (no action required) whenever the inquisitor is about to die as a result of an enemy’s attack or spell.

Office of Renewal

Many faiths profess the concept of cyclical change in both the material plane and the planes beyond. No one, not even the gods, are immune to the everpresent changes of life and death, creation and destruction.

Inquisitors serving in this office live in spiritual accordance with this view, and do their part to ensure the smooth and constant balance of this cosmic cycle.

Karma (Su)

There is no cause without effect, and effects can ripple throughout eternity. As a swift action, an legendary inquisitor can share a harmful effect with a creature within 30 feet who harmed her.

This harmful effect can come in the form of hit point damage, a negative effect from a spell, or some other harm caused by the target’s actions. If the effect allowed a saving throw, the target can attempt the same save as the inquisitor.

An legendary inquisitor can use this ability once per day. At 4th level and every three levels thereafter, the inquisitor can use this ability one additional time per day.

Vicious Cycle (Su)

At 8th level, when the inquisitor activates her bane ability, she can grant her weapon the vicious magic weapon ability instead of bane.

Reincarnation (Sp)

At 16th level, an legendary inquisitor adds reincarnation as a 4th level spell and raise dead as a 5th level spell to her list of spells known.

Humbling Renewal (Sp)

At 17th level, an legendary inquisitor can transform a defeated enemy into a small animal, as per the baleful polymorph spell. The enemy must be helpless and at negative hit points (no save). The legendary inquisitor can use this ability a number of times per day equal to 3 + her Wisdom bonus.

Forced Reincarnation (Su)

At 20th level, the inquisitor gains the Forced Reincarnation grand hex, treating her legendary inquisitor level as her witch level. She cannot use this ability on the same creature more than once per day.

Office of Scriptures

Many inquisitors believe in the power of the written word.

Holy and revered scriptures have to be protected and preserved at any cost, while heretical and obscene texts or subversive leaflets must be destroyed or hoarded away from the sight of common people, lest they harm their faith or put their mind under control. Or the other way round.

Sacred Scripture (Ex)

Once per day when she regains spells, the inquisitor can bond with a book, a scroll, or other written item. This functions as the sacred bond ability (see below). In addition, while she is wielding her sacred scripture with at least one hand, the inquisitor gains a bonus equal to her Wisdom modifier to Spellcraft checks made to counterspell. A number of times per day equal to her Wisdom bonus, the inquisitor can counter an enemy’s spell without sacrificing one of her spell slots. For every 3 levels the inquisitor possesses, she can use this latter ability 1 additional time per day.

Words of Power (Sp)

At 8th level, the inquisitor adds the following spells to her known spells list at the indicated spell levels: book ward (2nd), commune with texts (6th), mage’s perusal (1st), memorize page (1st), open book (2nd), page-bound epiphany (3rd), parchment swarm (4th), scrivener’s chant (0), secluded grimoire (1st), sealed sending (5th), and skim (1st).

Censure Apocrypha (Su)

At 16th level, the inquisitor gains Improved Counterspell as a bonus feat. She can also try to counterspell permanent magic writings by attempting a counterspell check against the item’s caster level. Upon a successful check, the target writing is totally destroyed unless it succeeds at an item Will saving throw.

Epiphany (Su)

At 17th level, the inquisitor can use every written magic item she bonded with, regardless of prerequisites. Once per day, she can also use one of her spell slots to cast a spell contained in her bonded sacred scripture that is of a level she could normally cast, even if that spell is not in the inquisitor spell list. A spell cast this way is considered a divine spell, and is not erased from a scroll or spellbook.

Logos (Sp)

At 20th level, the inquisitor considers every life as a book rich in knowledge and information. She can use scribe’s binding once per day as a spell-like ability.

Office of Tithes

A church’s finances need to be administered, and some priests feel too pure to “get their hands dirty” with vile money. So it’s often one of the inquisitors’ duties to collect alms and donations and see that they are put to a good use (whatever this may mean for their religion).

Tithing Fund (Ex)

The legendary inquisitor endeavors to be prepared for any situation. As a result, she may carry unspecified equipment worth up to 100 gp per class level. This can be any kind of gear that can reasonably fit into a backpack, including potions and scrolls or other small and portable magic items (such magic items must have been created by a divine spellcaster). As a full-round action, the inquisitor may dig through her pockets to retrieve an item she specifies at that time, deducting its value from the allocated amount of cost. This item cannot weigh more than 10 pounds. When the total remaining cost reaches 0, the inquisitor can retrieve no more items until she refills her tithing fund by spending a few hours and an equivalent amount of gold to bring her total up to 100 gp per class level.

In addition, if she takes 1 hour to pack her gear each day as part of her daily prayers or meditation for spells, the inquisitor gains a +4 bonus to Strength to determine her light encumbrance. This does not affect her maximum carrying capacity. The efficient distribution of weight simply encumbers her less than the same amount of weight normally should. Finally, the inquisitor gains a +4 bonus on Sleight of Hand checks made to conceal small objects on her person.

Donation Plate (Su)

At 8th level, as a full round action, the inquisitor can transmute a single object that is not an artifact into a number of gold pieces equal to the item’s price. She can use this ability once per week.

Charitable (Ex)

At 16th level, the inquisitor gains a reputation for being charitable, if not generous, toward the right people.

She adds her Wisdom bonus to Bluff and Diplomacy checks and Charisma ability checks in addition to her Charisma bonus.

Commission Weapon (Ex)

At 17th level, the inquisitor can commission a single magic weapon for her personal use. She only needs to pay 1/2 price for this magic weapon (cost). This is a one-time ability and can be reserved for a future level, if so desired.

Escalier to the Planes (Sp)

At 20th level, the inquisitor can literally buy her way into Heaven (or any other plane). She can use gate as a spell-like ability once per day, but must still pay the material cost of the spell.

Office of Trials

Inquisitors from this office actively search and unmask creatures from enemy alignments and faiths. A trial can also be used to determine whether a target is guilty of a crime.

Trial

As a standard action, an legendary inquisitor can declare a trial against one creature within 30 ft. At 1st level, she can declare a trial once per day. At 4th level and every three levels thereafter, the inquisitor can use this ability one additional time per day.

When the inquisitor declares a trial, she must select one trial type. Every trial is a curse effect. A trial only works on a target if its alignment is not within one step of the inquisitor’s deity.

Additionally, if the target fails its saving throw against a trial and has an element of its alignment that is in direct opposition to the inquisitor’s (chaos opposes law and evil opposes good), she can also attempt an Intimidate check to demoralize the target as a free action.

A trial’s duration is 1 minute (even if the inquisitor can end it first if she wishes), except for trial by element that is an instantaneous effect.

Trial by Balance (Su)

Even simple, unliving items and tools refuse to be used by a miscreant. Every round, a target must succeed at a Reflex save or drop whatever item it holds in its hands.

Trial By Beast (Su)

An animal appears to combat the target, as per summon nature’s ally I, with a caster level equal to 1/2 the inquisitor’s level (minimum 1). Only one creature can be summoned this way. At 3rd level, and every 2 levels thereafter, the power of this ability increases by one spell level, allowing to summon more powerful creatures (to a maximum of summon nature’s ally IX at 17th level).

Trial By Blood (Su)

The target takes 1 point of bleed per round, plus one additional point of bleed at levels 7 and 14.

The legendary inquisitor can use blood biography on the target once (1 question only) at any moment while the target is bleeding.

Trial By Corsned (Sp)

The legendary inquisitor offers the target a blessed consumable item that the target is forced to consume, as per the beguiling gift spell. A guilty target will be choked by the blessed food or drink and follows the rules for suffocation.

Trial By Element (Su)

The legendary inquisitor selects acid, cold, electricity, or fire. The targeted opponent suffers 1d6 points of damage, plus another 1d6 for every three levels of the inquisitor beyond 1st. Half the damage is energy damage of the chosen type, but the other half results directly from divine power and is therefore not subject to being reduced by energy resistance.

Trial By Iron (Ex)

Any damage reduction the target possesses becomes DR/cold iron for the duration of the trial.

Trial By Ordeal (Ex)

The legendary inquisitor can challenge an opponent to single combat. This works as the cavalier’s challenge ability, using the inquisitor’s base attack bonus as her cavalier level.

Trial By Poison (Ex)

The target takes 1 point of Constitution damage per round until they make a successful save. At 10th level, this becomes Constitution drain.

Trial By Water (Su)

If the target is immersed in a body of water, it takes a -10 penalty on all Swim checks and loses the amphibious quality and the benefits of the water subtype if it possessed them. If the target is on land, it suffers instead the effects of cup of dust, except that it must attempt a new saving throw once per round to contrast the effects of dehydration. A target whose alignment is within one step of the inquisitor’s deity is instead granted a water walk effect.

Abridged Trial (Su)

At 8th level, an legendary inquisitor can use her trial ability as a swift action.

Instant Trial (Su)

At 16th level, an legendary inquisitor can use her trial ability as a free action, but no more than once per round.

Unerring Trial (Su)

At 17th level, select one type of trial that allows a saving throw. The Difficulty Class of this save is increased by 3.

Adjournment (Su)

At 20th level, targets of an inquisitor’s trial ability must roll twice on a saving throw and choose the lower result.

Other Alternate Class Options
Replaces Bane/Greater Bane…
Alchemical Avenger (Su)

At 5th level, the inquisitor learns to create alchemically powered arrows, bolts, or bullets which can be used to destroy her enemies. She may create a number of such projectiles per day equal to her class level + her Wisdom modifier. Creating each projectile takes 1 minute.

The DC for any saving throw against the effect of one of these projectiles is 10 + 1/2 the inquisitor’s class level + her Wisdom modifier.

When an arrow is created, the inquisitor chooses a special effect the arrow adds to its attack:

Acid: The projectile covers the target in acid. Unless the target uses a full-round action to remove the acid (which draws attacks of opportunity), they will take 1d6 acid damage per round for the next 3 rounds. At 12th level, this increases to 2d6 acid damage. While under the effects of the acid, a creature can not regain hit points.
Concussion: The projectile does an additional 1d10 sonic damage, and the target must make a Fortitude save or be deafened for 1 minute. At 12th level, the damage increases to 2d10.
Flame: The projectile does an additional 2d6 fire damage to a target it hits. This increases to 4d6 at 12th level. Those struck by the projectile are subject to a faerie fire effect that lasts 1 minute.
Heavy: The projectile does an additional 1d10 force damage, and the target must make a Reflex save or be knocked prone. This increases to 2d10 at 12th level.
Ice: The projectile does an additional 2d6 cold damage to a target it hits. This increases to 4d6 at 12th level.
Jinxing: A creature struck by this projectile has a -2 penalty to their AC for 1 minute. This penalty does not stack with itself. At 12th level, the penalty increases to -4.
Lightning: The projectile does an additional 2d6 electricity damage to a target it hits. This increases to 4d6 at 12th level. At 12th level, the inquisitor may also choose from the following options:
Enfeebling: Those struck by the projectile must make a Will save or be confused (as the confusion spell) for 1 round.
Flash: Those struck with the projectile must make a Fortitude save or be blinded for 1 round. This is a light effect.
Grounding: The projectile leaves a stain of heavy metal dust on a target it has successfully hit. The dust makes it difficult to move in unconventional ways. For the next minute, the target can not teleport or be teleported, can not pass through other objects (if incorporeal) and has a -20 penalty to all Fly skill checks.
Auspician (Sp)

At 5th level, the inquisitor can cast harrowing as a spell-like ability once per day. At 12th level, she can cast greater harrowing too as a spell-like ability once per day. The legendary inquisitor can choose to gain runecasting and greater runecasting instead of these.

Favored Weapon Training (Ex)

At 5th level, the inquisitor gains proficiency with all weapons in one fighter weapon group that includes her deity’s favored weapon. In addition, whenever she attacks with a weapon from this group, she gains a +1 bonus on attack and damage rolls. This bonus increases by +1 at levels 9, 13, and 17. At 12th level, the inquisitor gains Weapon Specialization as a bonus feat, even if she does not meet the requirements. This feat is applied to her deity’s favored weapon.

Fire and Sword (Su)

At 5th level, the inquisitor can bring down her enemies with fire and sword (or some other combination of energy damage and weapon). As a swift action, she can grant herself a +2 sacred or profane bonus to attack rolls while imbuing her weapon with an energy damage type selected from the list below. Once this energy type is chosen, it cannot be changed without divine intervention. Inquisitors who are good or serve a good deity gain a sacred bonus. Inquisitors who are evil or serve an evil deity gain a profane bonus. Neutral inquisitors of neutral deities must choose between sacred and profane. Once this choice is made it cannot be changed. This bonus to attack rolls only applies to attacks made with the imbued weapon. This ability only functions while the inquisitor wields the weapon.

If dropped or taken, the weapon resumes granting this ability if it is returned to the inquisitor before the duration expires.

This ability lasts for a number of rounds per day equal to the inquisitor’s level. These rounds do not need to be consecutive.

When an legendary inquisitor uses her fire and sword ability, the additional energy damage does not stack with magic weapon special abilities that have a matching energy type. This extra damage is not multiplied on a critical hit. Typically, an legendary inquisitor will choose an energy type that corresponds with a domain of her deity.

At 12th level, the inquisitor’s fire and sword damage increases, as per the list below.

Table 3-1: Energy Damage
Energy Damage Type	5th Level Additional Damage	12th Level Additional Damage
Acid	2d6	4d6

Fire and sword is treated as bane for the purpose of prerequisites and interacting with feats. The Spell Bane feat allows to inflict penalties to creatures vulnerable to the chosen element or with the opposite elemental subtype.

Fortuity (Su)

At 5th level, the inquisitor can call upon her deity to grant her good fortune in trying times. As a swift action, she gains a +2 luck bonus to AC, skill and ability checks, and saving throws for 1 round per legendary inquisitor level per day. These need not be consecutive. This luck bonus increases by 1 at levels 10, 15, and 20. At 12 level, the luck bonus from the inquisitor’s fortuity ability also applies to attacks and damage rolls.

Replaces Cunning Initiative…
Combat Insight (Ex)

The legendary inquisitor adds her Wisdom bonus to her base attack bonus and size bonus when determining her Combat Maneuver Bonus instead of her Strength or Dexterity bonus.

Cynical Initiative (Ex)

The legendary inquisitor always acts during surprise rounds.

Defense Insight (Ex)

The legendary inquisitor adds her Wisdom bonus to her Armor Class and Combat Maneuver Defense in addition to her Dexterity bonus.

Divine Skirmisher (Ex)

The legendary inquisitor gains Weapon Finesse as a bonus feat and can use it with her deity’s favored weapon, even if it is not a light weapon.

Replaces Detect Alignment…
Arcane Seer (Sp)

The legendary inquisitor can use greater detect magic at will, as the spell.

Detect Enemies of the Faith (Sp)

The legendary inquisitor can use detect outsider at will. She can only detect creatures with an alignment opposite to her deity’s.

Detect Undead (Sp)

The legendary inquisitor can detect undead at will, as the spell.

Eye For Intrigue (Sp)

The legendary inquisitor can use detect anxieties, detect desires, detect relations, and sense fear at will. She can only use one of these at any given time.

Hidden Ways (Sp)

The legendary inquisitor can detect secret doors at will, as the spell.

Querier (Sp)

At 2nd level, the inquisitor receives a bonus talent of her choice from the Divination sphere. The legendary inquisitor is always considered to possess the Fate sphere for the purpose of bonus alternate divinations.

Sensitive (Sp)

The legendary inquisitor can detect thoughts at will, as the spell.

Replaces Discern Lies…
Appraiser (Sp)

An legendary inquisitor can cast discern value for a number of rounds per day equal to her legendary inquisitor level.

These rounds do not need to be consecutive. Activating this ability is an immediate action.

Inquirer (Sp)

At 2nd level, the inquisitor gains Truth (from the Fate sphere) as a bonus talent. If the inquisitor has not access to the Fate sphere yet, she gains Fate as a bonus sphere too, with the Tongue of Ages drawback.

Pieces and Scraps (Sp)

An legendary inquisitor with the eye for intrigue ability can cast hypercognition for a number of rounds per day equal to her legendary inquisitor level. These rounds do not need to be consecutive. Activating this ability is an immediate action.

Thoughtsense (Sp)

An legendary inquisitor with the dilettante mystic ability can cast thoughtsense for a number of rounds per day equal to her legendary inquisitor level. These rounds do not need to be consecutive. Activating this ability is an immediate action.

Replaces Domain…
Church Knight (Ex)

At 1st level, the inquisitor selects a cavalier’s order. She gains bonus skills and must obey her order’s edict as a cavalier but doesn’t gain the order’s special challenge. At 2nd and 8th level, the inquisitor receives the appropriate abilities from her order.

Domain Familiar (Ex)

A deity can allow any of its servants with domains or inquisitions to replace one domain’s first-level power with a familiar. This will most often take the form of the deity’s sacred animal, and is likely to have the Emissary familiar archetype, maybe even gaining the same domain power that its master forwent. The character can choose to gain Improved Familiar as a bonus feat at 8th level in place of her domain’s higher-level power.

Rogue Saint: Rather than a domain, the inquisitor chooses an oracle mystery granted by her deity. She gains one revelation from her chosen mystery at 1st level and another at 8th level. She must meet these revelations’ prerequisites, using her legendary inquisitor level as her effective oracle level to determine the revelations’ effects, and she never qualifies for the Extra Revelation feat. In addition, a rogue saint needs not have an alignment within one step of her deity.

Replaces Exploit Weakness…
Almighty Avoidance (Ex)

An legendary inquisitor who possesses the by the grace of, cunning dance, or stalwart ability can improve it in such a way that while the character still takes no damage on a successful saving throw against attacks, she henceforth takes only half damage on a failed save. A helpless legendary inquisitor does not gain the benefit of almighty avoidance.

Divine Renewal (Su)

Whenever the inquisitor casts an legendary inquisitor spell, she regains hit points equal to the level of the spell.

Hide in Plain Sight (Ex)

The legendary inquisitor can use Stealth to hide even when being observed. As long as she is within 10 feet of dim light (her own shadow doesn’t count), she can hide without anything to actually hide behind.

Replaces Monster Lore…
Congregation’s Secretary (Ex)

The legendary inquisitor gains the master scribe ability of the chronicler prestige class.

Dilettante Mystic (Ex)

The legendary inquisitor gains Psychic Sensitivity as a bonus feat.

Omens Reader (Ex)

The legendary inquisitor gains Cast Rune as a bonus feat. At 10th level, she also gains Improved Cast Rune.

Sacred Bond (Ex)

The legendary inquisitor forges a bond with a holy item of significance for her faith. This functions as a wizard’s arcane bond, except that the bonded item also works as the inquisitor’s holy symbol and divine focus.

Once per day, the inquisitor’s bonded item allows her to cast a spell from the inquisitor spell list that’s of a level she can cast, even if it isn’t one of her spells known. No character can have both a bonded item and a familiar at the same time.

Secret Champion (Ex)

The legendary inquisitor gains the vigilante’s dual identity ability, except that both her social and vigilante identity must have an alignment within one step from her deity’s.

Replaces Solo Tactics & Teamwork Feats…

Covert Agent: Instead of solo tactics, an legendary inquisitor with the secret champion ability gains the seamless guise vigilante ability. Every time she would gain a teamwork feat, she can select a social talent or vigilante talent as a vigilante of her same level.

Divine Touch (Su)

At 3rd level, an legendary inquisitor can deliver divine energy by touch. She can deliver either positive energy or negative energy. A good legendary inquisitor (or a neutral legendary inquisitor of a good deity) must select positive energy. An evil legendary inquisitor (or a neutral legendary inquisitor of an evil deity) must select negative energy. An legendary inquisitor who is neither good nor evil and whose deity is neither good nor evil can select either positive or negative energy. This choice is made when the inquisitor gains this ability and cannot be changed.

Each day the inquisitor can use this ability a number of times equal to half her legendary inquisitor level plus her Charisma modifier. With one use of this ability, an legendary inquisitor can use divine energy to restore to a target 1d6 hit points for every 2 legendary inquisitor levels she has. Using this ability is a standard action, unless the inquisitor targets herself, in which case it is a swift action. An legendary inquisitor who delivers negative energy with her touch can instead deal 1d6 points of damage to a living creature for every 2 legendary inquisitor levels she has. Alternatively, an legendary inquisitor can use this divine energy to affect undead creatures, dealing damage when delivering positive energy or restoring hit points when delivering negative energy.

An legendary inquisitor needs only one freehand to use this ability.

Using divine touch to harm a creature requires a successful melee touch attack and doesn’t provoke an attack of opportunity.

Creatures do not receive a saving throw against the damage from divine touch. Divine touch is modified by any feat, spell, or effect that specifically works with the lay on hands paladin class feature. For example, the Extra Lay On Hands feat grants an legendary inquisitor two additional uses of the divine touch class feature.

At 3rd level and every 3 levels thereafter, the inquisitor can select a mercy to add to this power if she delivers positive energy, or a cruelty if she delivers negative energy.

Hexenmeister: Instead of gaining solo tactics, the inquisitor gains Eldritch Secrets as a bonus feat at 3rd level. She can also select a witch hex in place of a teamwork feat every time she would gain one. At 12th level, she can select major hexes in place of teamwork feats.

Office Feats: Instead of solo tactics, the inquisitor gains a bonus feat with the judgment (or office) class feature as a prerequisite. Every time the inquisitor would gain a teamwork feat, she can instead select another such bonus feat.

Temple Raider: Instead of solo tactics, the inquisitor gains trapfinding at 3rd level. She also can select a rogue talent in place of a teamwork feat every time she would gain one. At 12th level, she can select advanced talents in place of teamwork feats.

Vampire Hunting: Instead of solo tactics, the inquisitor gains Vampire Hunter Tradition as a bonus feat. She also can select a vampire hunting technique feat in place of a teamwork feat every time she would gain one.

Replaces Stalwart…
By the Grace Of (Ex)

An legendary inquisitor can use a reserve of agility and grace to dance around physical attacks. If she makes a Fortitude or Reflex saving throw against an attack that has a reduced effect on a successful save, she instead avoids the effect entirely. This ability can only be used if the inquisitor is wearing light armor, medium armor, or no armor. A helpless legendary inquisitor does not gain the benefit of this ability.

Cultivated Tolerance (Ex)

The legendary inquisitor has trained her body with certain drugs and medicines to become immune to all poisons and the sickened condition.

Cunning Dance (Ex)

An legendary inquisitor can use a great coordination of perception and acrobatics to avoid both physical and mental attacks. If she makes a Reflex or Will saving throw against an attack that has a reduced effect on a successful save, she instead avoids the effect entirely. This ability can only be used if the inquisitor is wearing light armor, medium armor, or no armor. A helpless legendary inquisitor does not gain the benefit of this ability.

Impenetrable Faith (Ex)

The legendary inquisitor is immune to fear (magical or otherwise), as well as to compulsion spells and spell-like abilities.

Suffering Servant (Su)

The legendary inquisitor is able to withstand great amounts of physical punishment. Choose one alignment that opposes the inquisitor’s alignment (chaos, evil, good, or law). She gains DR 5/against attacks based on this alignment.

Replaces Stern Gaze…
Harrowing Touch (Sp)

The legendary inquisitor can cause a creature’s internal strength to fail them as a melee touch attack. The target receives a penalty to all saving throws equal to 1/2 the inquisitor’s level (minimum –1). This effect fades after 3 rounds. She can use this ability a number of times per day equal to 3 + her Wisdom modifier.

Preacher (Ex)

The legendary inquisitor achieves conversions easily with her inspired words. She gains a morale bonus equal to 1/2 her level on all Perform (oratory) skill checks and Perform (oratory) is a class skill for her.

Smooth Detective (Ex)

The legendary inquisitor is skilled at pinpointing clues and asking the right questions. She gains a morale bonus on all Diplomacy checks to gather information and Perception checks to notice creatures equal to 1/2 her legendary inquisitor level (minimum +1).

Divine Power

An legendary inquisitor that has access to a domain or subdomain adds that domain’s 1st- through 6th-level bonus spells to her known spells list at the appropriate levels.

Inquisitions
Free Will Inquisition

Granted Powers: Nothing can hinder your personal liberty-not even the world’s natural laws.

Mantle of Free Will (Sp)

Once per day, you can use suppress charms and compulsions as a spell-like ability.

Shatter Chains (Su)

At 8th level, when you activate your bane ability, you can choose for your weapon to instead gain the liberating weapon special ability.

Opposites Inquisition

Granted Powers: The opposite of “neither” is not “one or the other”, but “both”. Just because we consider some energies opposite to each other, it doesn’t mean they can’t work together.

Harmony of Contraries (Su)

Whenever you cast a spell with the acid, cold, electricity, or fire descriptor, you can convert half of the spell’s damage into its opposite energy type (acid is opposed to electricity and cold is opposed to fire).

Utraquality (Ex)

At 8th level, you gain Elemental Commixture as a bonus feat. Once per day as a swift action, you can also grant this feat to an ally within 30 feet of you. You can use this ability one more time per day for every 4 levels you possess beyond 8th.

Pacification Inquisition

Granted Powers: War and conflicts bring death, sorrow and poverty to the land. You have sworn to compose feuds, repress violence, and go to any lengths to preserve the common people’s peace.

Justice of Peace (Ex)

You gain Peacemaker as a bonus feat.

Quell the Flames (Sp)

At 4th level, you can cast calm emotions once per day as a spell-like ability, but only to negate or suppress negative emotion effects.

Treaty of Nonaggression (Su)

At 8th level, you can emit a 30-foot aura of nonviolence for a number of rounds per day equal to your cleric level. These rounds need not be consecutive. Creatures in this area that try to attack others take 2d6 points of nonlethal damage each round they attempt to harm another creature. Creatures that use violence to defend themselves or others do not suffer any damage.

Relentless Inquisition

Granted Powers: You deliver divine justice through your weapon, fusing spell and sword in one lethal judgment.

Divine Spell Strike (Su)

Whenever you cast an legendary inquisitor spell with a range of “touch”, you can deliver the spell through any weapon you are wielding as part of a melee attack. Instead of the free melee touch attack normally allowed to deliver the spell, you can make one free melee attack with your weapon (at your full base attack bonus) as part of casting this spell. If successful, this melee attack deals its normal damage as well as the effects of the spell. If the attack is a successful critical hit, the weapon does its normal increased damage, but the spell’s effects are unchanged.

Divine Spell Combat (Su)

At 8th level, when you make a full-round attack, you may replace one of the attacks you would normally make with your primary weapon at your highest base attack bonus with an legendary inquisitor spell. The spell chosen must be one which can normally be cast as a standard action.

Sagacity Inquisition

Granted Powers: You are a divine investigator, gathering information for the church’s offices.

Broad Education (Ex)

You use your Wisdom modifier instead of your Dexterity or Charisma modifier with any two skills of your choice.

Sudden Insight (Ex)

At 8th level, when attempting a skill check, you can roll twice and take the higher result. If you have an ability that allows you to roll twice, you cannot use that ability and this benefit on the same roll. You may use this ability a number of times per day equal to your Wisdom modifier.

Favored Class Bonuses

The following favored class bonuses are available to all characters, regardless of race:

Any: +1/2 faith point
Any: +1/2 damage and healing whenever you use channel energy
Any: +1 on Knowledge (religion or planes) checks
Any: +1/4 caster level on domain spells
Any: +1/5 saving throw DC of domain abilities and domain spells
Any: +1 bonus on caster level checks made to overcome the spell resistance of outsiders
Any: +1 bonus on concentration checks made to cast a legendary cleric spell
